thread:
samir: FYI starting a 5% canary for v3.2-int4-longctx (doc-summary workload) now. want a quick sanity on gating rules before we ramp.
elaine: nice — what's the primary risk vector here? latency or fidelity?
samir: both. longctx int4 reduced mem usage but we saw tail latency bumps on a small slice + a subtle drop in concordance for multi-paragraph summaries.
ryan: can we decouple the gates? e.g., separate latency window vs quality window so one can trigger a soft-throttle and the other triggers hard rollback.
elaine: +1. propose: latency gate = p95 > 220ms (vs baseline) for 3 consecutive 5-min windows -> soft-throttle (cut to 2%). quality gate = concordance delta <= -0.8% absolute OR MRR drop >0.5% -> immediate rollback.
samir: sounds good but add a sustained-degradation guard: quality delta > -0.4% for >=30m should pause ramp (to 1%) not full rollback.
ryan: agree. also for longdocs add slice-specific thresholds: longdoc-concordance delta threshold tighter (-0.5%) since it's more visible.
ml-ops-bot: suggested autoscaling knobs: reduce batch_size by 20% under tail-latency pressure, enable kv-prefetch on warm paths.
natalie: can we codify this as a policy blob so releases and deploy-bot can enforce it? I can push the policy to gatebook if you give me the JSON.
samir: putting a draft config below — feel free to tweak. this is what deploy-bot should read for canary decisions.
```json
{ "canary_percent": 5, "windows": {"short": 300, "long": 1800}, "latency_gate": {"metric": "p95_latency_ms", "threshold_delta": 20, "action": "soft_throttle", "consecutive_windows": 3}, "quality_gate": {"metric": "concordance_pct", "threshold_delta": -0.8, "action": "rollback", "sustained_pause_delta": -0.4, "sustained_minutes": 30}, "slice_overrides": {"longdoc": {"quality_threshold_delta": -0.5}}, "auto_mitigation": {"reduce_batch_pct": 20, "enable_kv_prefetch": true}, "rollback_reason_whitelist": ["infrastructure", "model_hung"], "notify_channels": ["#eng-ml", "#oncall"] }
```
elaine: that looks clean. question: concordance metric — use anchor-based scoring (baseline v3.1) or human-eval subset?
ryan: use anchor concordance for fast gating; backstop with periodic human-eval slices (hourly sample) and a concordance sanity job.
samir: deploy-bot can we wire this so if quality_gate triggers, we immediately flip traffic to fallback-model (v3.1 quant) and create a P0 incident channel?
deploy-bot: ACK. will implement auto-flip to pinned_fallback when quality_gate.action == "rollback" and create incident thread with tag #auto-rollback.
ml-ops-bot: running initial stats — baseline p95=198ms, baseline concordance=92.4%. canary first 10k requests: p95=205ms, concordance=91.7% (delta -0.7%).
natalie: delta -0.7% sits in the warning zone. keep at 5% for 30m, sample human-eval for 200 longdocs.
samir: agreed. if we cross -0.8% -> rollback. if tail latency breaches 220ms for 3 windows -> throttle to 2% then re-evaluate.
elaine: also add an escape hatch: if user-facing error rate >0.1% absolute increase, immediate rollback irrespective of other gates.
ryan: noted. I'll update gatebook policy and add smokecheck to the release job.
samir: thanks — we'll monitor. ping here with the 30m summary and we'll decide ramp or rollback. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
